newsitem.title: TAIWAN: TAIWAN CENTRAL BANK INJECTS T$15 BLN IN FUND.
newsitem.headline: TAIWAN CENTRAL BANK INJECTS T$15 BLN IN FUND.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank, responding to rising money rates on tight liquidity, injected T$15 billion worth of funds into the banking system through open market operations on Monday, a central bank official said.
The bank executed a repurchase of negotiable certificates of deposit, treasury bills and government bonds offered by interested financial institutions with a rate of 8.40-8.75 percent.
The institutions have the option of repurchasing the NCDs, treasury bills and government bonds within 30 days, the official said.
At 0400 GMT, the overnight interbank rate was at 9.697 percent against Saturday's 9.525 finish -- well above the central bank's 5.0-5.5 percent target zone.
